items.comment: Accurate: `into[T] >: T = T` means only `T <: into[T]` is visible outside the opaque scope, so `underlying` is genuinely the only way for external callers to go from `into[T]` back to `T`. The phrasing is just slightly awkward — 'revealing the opaque `into[T]` alias' reads as if the alias itself is being exposed, when what's actually revealed is the underlying representation type that the opaque alias hides. Consider something like 'Converts `x` from the opaque `into[T]` type to its underlying type `T`.' for clarity.
